title: A second monthly lag gave a small and block-sensitive sea-level forecast gain at 217 gauges in 2010-2024
abstract: We tested a second monthly residual lag against first-order decay in December-origin sea-level forecasts. We used a fixed PSMSL archive, 217 gauges and 38,072 monthly targets in 2010-2024. Each fit used 20 prior years. The second lag reduced full-year mean squared error by 0.437%. Conditional 95% three-year block limits were 0.039% to 0.780%. RMSE fell from 92.770 to 92.568 mm. The one-year block interval included zero. A post-score test held decay shape fixed and removed the starting November-to-December change. The measured change gave a 0.141% gain, with limits of -0.249% to 0.515%. The small main gain does not establish a distinct value for recent motion or a physical recovery law. Revised data, uneven coverage, December-only origins and short conditional tests limit inference. Original code, source hashes, aggregate scores, resampling indices, audits and a figure are included. Source records and derived record-level tables remain external.

display.caption: AR2 forecast MSE reduction against AR1 at December origins in 2010-2024. Positive values mean lower error. Conditional limits use three-year blocks shared across gauges. Quarter and lead change together.

citations.reason: Published decay benchmark sets source and sample rules. New code tests a second residual lag. Data overlap; this is not independent confirmation.
